The threat actor executed malicious code via a scheduled task on domain controller DC-01 (10.0.8.200), establishing C2 communication with 198.51.100.77 over HTTPS. Lateral movement observed from workstation WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) using Cobalt Strike beacons. Containment actions include blocking C2 IPs and credential revocation.

timeline.description: Initial access via spearphishing attachment opened by user CORP\jsmith on WS-FIN-042.
Execution: rundll32.exe launched from Temp directory, indicative of code execution.
C2 beaconing detected to 198.51.100.23 (Cobalt Strike) and confirmed to 198.51.100.77 (known APT-29 infrastructure).
Lateral movement attempt via Kerberos TGT request from WS-FIN-042 to internal server.
SMB-based lateral movement to file server WS-FIN-050 confirmed.
Alert generated for persistence activity on domain controller DC-01 via scheduled task (T1053.005).
Containment: C2 IP 198.51.100.77 blocked at firewall; credentials for CORP\jsmith revoked.
Eradication: WS-FIN-042 isolated and full forensic scan initiated.

arguments.summary: APT-29 (Cozy Bear) campaign detected leveraging spearphishing (T1566.001) to compromise user endpoint, execute malicious payload via rundll32, establish persistence through scheduled task on domain controller (10.0.8.200), and initiate C2 beaconing to known malicious IP 198.51.100.77 over HTTPS. Lateral movement observed via SMB and Kerberos exploitation. Account CORP\jsmith compromised and used for privilege escalation and internal reconnaissance. Immediate containment actions included blocking C2 IP at firewall, full EPP scan of domain controller (detecting ransomware variant), and revocation of all sessions and API keys for compromised user.

IDS alerts on Cobalt Strike beaconing from WS-FIN-042 to 198.51.100.23.
Failed Kerberos TGT requests from WS-FIN-042 indicating attempted privilege escalation.
Lateral movement via SMB to file server (10.0.5.50) from WS-FIN-042.
C2 beaconing detected from domain controller (10.0.8.200) to 198.51.100.77. Incident escalated.
Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to 198.51.100.77.
EPP full scan initiated on 10.0.8.200; detects 'Ransomware.WannaCry.Gen' in user profile.
IAM system revokes all active sessions and API keys for CORP\jsmith.

arguments.summary: Malware infection identified on endpoint 10.0.6.88 (user: CORP\auser) involving a packed UPX binary with anti-VM detection. The malware performed DNS tunneling to exfiltrate data to the domain data-exfil.evil.com. No malicious behavior was observed during sandbox analysis, likely due to evasion techniques. Incident declared contained. Post-incident review and reporting initiated.

rule Packed_UPX_With_AntiVM {
    meta:
        description = "Detects UPX-packed binaries exhibiting common anti-VM artifacts"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "INC-2026-1302"
        date = "2026-04-11"
        hash = "abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890"
    strings:
        $upx = { 55 50 58 20 50 61 63 6B 65 72 20 2A 2A 2A } // "UPX *" signature
        $anti_vm_bios = "VMware" ascii

    condition:
        $upx and ($anti_vm_bios or $anti_vm_reg)

arguments.summary: Malware infection detected on endpoint 10.0.6.88 (user CORP\auser) involving a UPX-packed binary with anti-VM evasion. The malware performed DNS tunneling to data-exfil.evil.com and attempted enumeration of financial records. Response actions included blocking the malicious domain at the firewall, resetting the user's credentials and MFA, and quarantining the threat via EPP. No data exfiltration was confirmed, but detection gaps were identified in initial EDR and sandbox analysis.

timeline.description: Initial alert triggered by malware analysis on endpoint 10.0.6.88. Static analysis reveals UPX-packed binary with anti-VM checks.
EDR queried for process tree and network connections on 10.0.6.88. Chrome.exe (PID 3200) observed connecting to 142.250.80.46:443.
SIEM search reveals 23 DNS queries to data-exfil.evil.com over past 7 days. No prior alerts generated.
Sandbox analysis returns 'clean' verdict with risk score 0.8. IOC extraction failed due to anti-analysis techniques.
Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to 142.250.80.46 and domain data-exfil.evil.com.
EPP full scan detects and quarantines Miner.CoinHive.A in /tmp/.x11-lock.
User CORP\auser's password and MFA token reset. Secure enrollment link sent to recovery email.
Incident declared contained. Post-incident review initiated.

rule Packed_UPX_With_AntiVM {
    meta:
        description = "Detects UPX-packed executables with common anti-VM artifacts"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "https://www.virusbulletin.com/vb2017/papers/pepackingdetection/"
        date = "2026-04-11"
        hash = "1b7a4244"
    strings:
        $upx = { 55 50 58 21 } // 'UPX!' header
        $anti_vm_strings = "VMACOS" fullword ascii
        $section_name_obf = "..upx" nocase
    condition:
        $upx at 0 and any of ($anti_vm_strings, $section_name_obf)
}

arguments.summary: Ongoing monitoring of suspicious activity originating from host WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15) in the IT department. Initial alerts indicated network scanning behavior from external source 10.0.8.200, which was later associated with benign traffic. However, a full endpoint scan revealed the presence of cryptocurrency mining malware (Miner.CoinHive.A) on WS-IT-101. No evidence of lateral movement or data exfiltration was found. The host is used by the helpdesk team and is of low criticality.

timeline.description: External IP 10.0.8.200 triggered IDS alert 'ET SCAN Nmap SYN Scan' targeting WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). Action: logged.
Successful authentication to WS-IT-101 by user CORP\helpdesk.
Ongoing monitoring initiated for potential APT activity on network segment 10.0.8.0/24.
EDR query shows WS-IT-101 establishing outbound HTTPS connection to 142.250.80.46 (Google). No suspicious process or file activity detected at that time.
UEBA analysis returns low anomaly score (0.35) for user activity on WS-IT-101; no behavioral red flags.
SIEM search reveals historical port scan from 192.168.1.100 to WS-IT-101, blocked by firewall. Also confirms normal login by helpdesk user.
Sandbox analysis of file from WS-IT-101 returns 'clean' verdict with risk score 0.8, no IOCs extracted.
EPP/AV full scan of WS-IT-101 detects and quarantines cryptocurrency miner (Miner.CoinHive.A) from /tmp/.x11-lock.
Firewall isolation attempt denied by consensus. IAM privilege revocation attempt also denied.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Linux Cryptominer Process in Temporary Directory
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    - process_name: '/tmp/*'
    - process_name: '/var/tmp/*'
    - process_name: '/dev/shm/*'
  hash_blacklist:
    - field: process_hash_sha256
      value: a5c063c1d85a8c17dad444a4f3e7b8c9e0f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5
  condition: selection and hash_blacklist
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0196/
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate applications temporarily stored in /tmp
author: SOC Team

arguments.summary: An APT intrusion was detected originating from workstation WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42), initially accessed via a phishing email leading to PowerShell-based code execution and Cobalt Strike beaconing. The threat actor performed lateral movement via SMB and attempted Kerberos TGT requests. Immediate actions included user credential reset, endpoint hardening via Ansible, and full EPP scan. No evidence of data exfiltration was found. The source IP in the initial alert (10.0.5.14) was a misattribution; the true compromised host was 10.0.5.42.

IDS alert triggered: 'ET TROJAN Cobalt Strike Beacon C2 Activity' from WS-FIN-042.
Failed Kerberos TGT request from WS-FIN-042, indicating credential access attempt.
Lateral movement detected via SMB access from WS-FIN-042 to file server WS-FIN-050.
Incident response initiated based on ongoing monitoring alert for APT activity.
User 'jsmith@corp.local' credentials (password and MFA) reset; secure enrollment link sent.
Full EPP scan completed on WS-FIN-042; one Linux dropper detected in isolated context (likely false positive or test artifact).
Windows workstation hardening playbook applied to WS-FIN-042 via Ansible: disabled unnecessary services, enforced AppLocker, updated firewall rules.

arguments.summary: A credential compromise incident originating from a spear-phishing email led to the execution of a Cobalt Strike beacon on workstation WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42). The attacker leveraged PowerShell and rundll32.exe for execution and established command and control (C2) communication via HTTPS to a known malicious IP (198.51.100.23). Lateral movement was attempted via SMB to a finance file server. Indicators confirm persistence mechanisms, defense evasion, and data collection. The compromised user account (CORP\jsmith) was reset, the host was remediated via automated playbook, and a critical system library exploit was detected during scanning.

timeline.description: Legitimate Outlook process (outlook.exe) started by user CORP\jsmith.
Malicious encoded PowerShell command launched from Outlook, indicative of phishing payload execution (T1566.001).
Cobalt Strike beacon DLL (beacon.dll) dropped to user's Temp directory.
rundll32.exe executed the beacon DLL from Temp, establishing initial foothold (T1218.011).
Hosts file modified to block security-related domains (T1565.001).
IDS detected outbound C2 beacon traffic to 198.51.100.23 on TCP/443 (ET TROJAN Cobalt Strike Beacon C2 Activity).
Failed Kerberos TGT request, indicating potential credential misuse or Kerberoasting attempt.
Successful SMB access to finance file server (10.0.5.50), confirming lateral movement.
Post-incident root cause analysis initiated.
Compromised user account (CORP\jsmith) password and MFA token reset.
Automated remediation playbook executed on WS-FIN-042, removing persistence and isolating host.
Full EPP scan detected and quarantined 'Exploit.CVE-2024-3094' in system library.

title: Suspicious rundll32 Execution from User Temp Directory
id: 5a7b9c1d-2f3e-4a8b-9c1d-2f3e4a8b9c1d
description: Detects rundll32.exe loading a DLL from a user's Temp directory, a common technique for executing payloads.
status: experimental
author: SOC Team
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1218/011/
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1218.011
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith: '\\rundll32.exe'
        OriginalFileName: 'rundll32.exe'
        Description: 'Windows host process (Rundll32)'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'AppData\\Local\\Temp'
            - 'AppData\\Roaming'
            - '\\Temp\\'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate software updates (rare)
level: high

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Dropped_DLL {
    meta:
        description = "Detects Cobalt Strike beacon payloads often dropped to disk."
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/"
        date = "2026-04-11"
        hash = "a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2"
    strings:
        $beacon_config = { 2E 63 6F 6E 66 69 67 } // ".config" section common in beacons
        $useragent = "Mozilla/" wide ascii
        $https_get = "GET" nocase
        $c2_mutex = "Global\\\\MSCTF.Asm.{" ascii
    condition:
        uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and // MZ header
        filesize < 500KB and
        all of ($beacon_config, $useragent, $https_get) and
        $c2_mutex
}

arguments.summary: A credential compromise incident originating from a spear-phishing email led to the execution of Cobalt Strike Beacon on a high-criticality finance workstation (WS-FIN-042). The attacker used encoded PowerShell to drop and execute a malicious DLL via rundll32, establishing C2 communication to an external IP. Post-compromise activities included lateral movement attempts via SMB, host file modification, and scheduled task creation for persistence. The user's credentials and MFA token were reset, the host was fully scanned and remediated via playbook, and all malicious artifacts were addressed.

timeline.description: Legitimate Outlook session initiated by user CORP\jsmith.
Encoded PowerShell command launched from Outlook, indicative of malicious macro or link execution (T1566.001).
Malicious DLL 'beacon.dll' written to user's Temp directory.
rundll32.exe executed to load beacon.dll from Temp directory (T1218.011).
Hosts file modified to block security domains (T1565.001).
IDS detected outbound Cobalt Strike beacon to known C2 server 198.51.100.23 (T1071.001).
Failed Kerberos TGT request indicates potential credential dumping attempt.
Successful SMB access to file server (WS-FIN-050), confirming lateral movement (T1021.002).
Post-incident root cause analysis initiated. Incident formally declared.
User 'jsmith@corp.local' credentials and MFA token reset via IAM system.
Full EPP scan executed on WS-FIN-042; one exploit detected in third-party library.
Ansible remediation playbook 'remediate_cobalt_strike.yml' executed successfully, removing persistence mechanisms and isolating host.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious rundll32 Execution from User Temp Directory
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
  
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\\rundll32.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '%TEMP%'
      - '%AppData%'
      - '%LocalAppData%'
  condition: selection
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1218/011/
description: Detects rundll32 loading DLLs from user-writable directories, commonly used for living-off-the-land attacks.
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software updates (rare)
author: SOC Team

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Dll
{
    meta:
        description = "Detects Cobalt Strike Beacon DLL in memory or on disk"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/"
        date = "2026-04-11"
        hash = "a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2"

    strings:
        $beacon_config = { 2E 72 63 64 2E 64 61 74 } // ".rcd.dat"
        $http_get = "GET / HTTP/1.1" wide ascii
        $useragent = "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT" wide ascii
        $c2_mutex = "Global\\\\MSCTF.Asm.{" wide ascii

    condition:
        uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and all of them
}

arguments.summary: An APT actor gained initial access via a compromised finance workstation (WS-FIN-042, IP: 10.0.5.42) belonging to user CORP\jsmith. The host exhibited Cobalt Strike beaconing to an external C2 (198.51.100.23) and engaged in lateral movement via SMB to other internal systems. A network scan from 10.0.8.200 was also observed, though the host (WS-IT-101) showed no signs of compromise. Immediate containment actions included blocking the infected host at the firewall, resetting the user's credentials and MFA, performing a full EPP scan which detected a Linux dropper (likely false positive or dual-use tool), and applying a hardening playbook to the workstation.

arguments.summary: An APT actor compromised user CORP\jsmith via a phishing email, leading to execution of a Cobalt Strike beacon on host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42). The beacon initiated C2 communication to 198.51.100.23, performed internal reconnaissance, and attempted lateral movement via SMB. The threat was detected through IDS alerts and EDR telemetry. Response actions included host isolation, user credential reset, full system scan, and automated remediation via Ansible. No data exfiltration was confirmed.

timeline.description: User CORP\jsmith launched Outlook.exe on WS-FIN-042.
Malicious PowerShell executed from Outlook context with encoded command.
rundll32.exe loaded unsigned beacon.dll from Temp directory.
IDS detected Cobalt Strike beacon C2 traffic to 198.51.100.23:443.
Failed Kerberos TGT request from WS-FIN-042 indicating credential misuse attempt.
SMB access to file server 10.0.5.50 detected, indicating lateral movement.
Incident response initiated; monitoring confirmed ongoing APT activity.
Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic from 10.0.5.42.
User CORP\jsmith password and MFA token reset via IAM system.
Full EPP scan detected and quarantined malicious liblzma.so.5 (CVE-2024-3094).
Ansible playbook 'remediate_cobalt_strike.yml' executed successfully on WS-FIN-042.

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Dll
{
    meta:
        description = "Detects memory-resident Cobalt Strike beacon DLL"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/"
        tlp = "amber"
        miter_techniques = ["T1071.001", "T1218.011"]
    strings:
        $a = { FF E0 } // JMP RAX
        $b = "Windows Error Reporting" wide
        $c = "user32.dll" wide
        $d = "kernel32.dll" wide
        $e = { 68 ?? ?? ?? ?? 68 ?? ?? ?? ?? E8 ?? ?? ?? ?? 83 C4 08 } // PUSH DWORD, CALL
    condition:
        uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and all of them
}
